title: Unit 2 Mixed Review Core Test
description: Review book Unit 2: dilations, scale factor, similar figures, similar triangles, AA similarity, constant slope, rate of change, and graph slope.

questions.questionText: A point (3, 4) is dilated from the origin by scale factor 2. What is the image point?
questions.explanation: A dilation from the origin multiplies both coordinates by 2.

questions.questionText: A point (1, 5) is dilated from the origin by scale factor 3. What is the image point?
questions.explanation: A dilation from the origin multiplies both coordinates by 3.

questions.questionText: Two similar figures have corresponding sides 4 and 8. A matching side on the first figure is 6. What is the side on the second figure?
options: 12 units
10 units
3 units
14 units
questions.correctAnswer: 12 units
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 8 / 4 = 2. Multiply 6 by 2.

questions.questionText: Figure A has side lengths 3 and 5. Figure B has corresponding side lengths 6 and 10. What can you conclude?
options: The figures must be congruent.
The figures cannot be similar because the sides differ.
The side ratios are consistent, so this supports similarity.
Only the longer sides matter.
questions.correctAnswer: The side ratios are consistent, so this supports similarity.
questions.explanation: Compare matching ratios: 3/6 and 5/10. Similar figures need one consistent scale relationship.

questions.questionText: Triangle R has angles 40 degrees and 70 degrees. Triangle S has angles 70 degrees and 70 degrees. Which statement is best?
options: The triangles are congruent by AA.
The triangles are similar by AA.
The triangles are similar only if their side lengths are equal.
The triangles are not similar because one angle is hidden.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles are similar by AA.
questions.explanation: The missing angles are 70 degrees and 40 degrees. AA needs two matching angle pairs.

questions.questionText: One slope triangle has rise 2 and run 3. Another has rise 4 and run 6. What does this show?
options: The larger triangle is always steeper.
The slope is found by adding rise and run.
The triangles prove the line is horizontal.
The triangles have the same rise/run ratio, so they can represent the same line slope.
questions.correctAnswer: The triangles have the same rise/run ratio, so they can represent the same line slope.
questions.explanation: Compare 2/3 and 4/6. Constant slope means the ratios match, not that the triangles are the same size.

questions.questionText: A quantity changes from 10 to 22 in 3 hours. What is the rate of change?
options: 4 per hour
7.3 per hour
15 per hour
questions.correctAnswer: 4 per hour
questions.explanation: Rate of change is change in output divided by change in input: (22 - 10) / 3 = 4.

questions.questionText: A line passes through (1, 2) and (4, 8). What is its slope?
questions.explanation: Slope is rise over run: (8 - 2) / (4 - 1) = 6/3, which simplifies to 2.

questions.questionText: Two similar figures have corresponding sides 5 and 15. A matching side on the first figure is 7. What is the side on the second figure?
options: 17 units
21 units

questions.explanation: The scale factor is 15 / 5 = 3. Multiply 7 by 3.

questions.questionText: A line passes through (0, 1) and (2, 5). What is its slope?

questions.questionText: One slope triangle has rise 6 and run 10. Another has rise 9 and run 16. What does this show?
options: The rise/run ratios differ, so they do not show the same constant slope.
The triangles have the same rise/run ratio, so they can represent the same line slope.
The triangles must be congruent.

questions.questionText: A line passes through (3, -1) and (9, 7). What is its slope?
questions.explanation: Slope is rise over run: (7 - -1) / (9 - 3) = 8/6, which simplifies to 4/3.

questions.questionText: A student says a dilation by 3 makes every angle three times as large. Which response is best?
options: Yes. Every measurement triples under a dilation.
No. Dilations preserve length but change angles.
No. Dilations multiply lengths, but angle measures stay the same.
Yes, but only for triangles.
questions.correctAnswer: No. Dilations multiply lengths, but angle measures stay the same.
questions.explanation: Dilations change size while preserving shape, so side lengths scale but angle measures remain equal.

questions.questionText: A small triangle inside a larger triangle has one side parallel to the larger triangle's base. Why are the triangles similar?
options: They are congruent because the bases are parallel.
They share one angle and have a second matching angle from parallel lines, so AA applies.
They are similar because all nested triangles are similar.
They are not similar unless all side lengths are measured.
questions.correctAnswer: They share one angle and have a second matching angle from parallel lines, so AA applies.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines create corresponding angle matches. With the shared angle, two angle pairs match.

questions.questionText: Two slope triangles on a line have rise/run ratios 6/9 and 10/15. What is the strongest conclusion?
options: The second triangle is steeper because 10 is larger than 6.
The slope changes because the triangles are different sizes.
The slope is 16/24 because rises and runs should be added.
Both simplify to 2/3, so they support a constant slope of 2/3.
questions.correctAnswer: Both simplify to 2/3, so they support a constant slope of 2/3.
questions.explanation: Equivalent rise/run ratios describe the same steepness, even when the slope triangles are different sizes.

questions.questionText: A graph shows points (1, 9), (4, 3), and (7, -3) on one line. What is the rate of change?
questions.explanation: Each time x increases by 3, y decreases by 6. The slope is -6/3 = -2.

questions.questionText: Two similar signs have perimeters 18 inches and 45 inches. A side on the smaller sign is 7 inches. What is the matching side on the larger sign?
options: 14 inches
34 inches
17.5 inches
70 inches
questions.correctAnswer: 17.5 inches
questions.explanation: Perimeters scale like side lengths. The scale factor is 45/18 = 2.5, so 7 * 2.5 = 17.5.

questions.questionText: A point is dilated from the origin to (12, -8). The scale factor was 4. What was the original point?
questions.explanation: Work backward by dividing both image coordinates by 4: (12/4, -8/4) = (3, -2).

questions.questionText: A line represents dollars earned over hours worked. Its slope is 18. What does that mean?
options: The worker starts with $18.
The worker earns $18 total.
The graph goes right 18 for every 1 up.
The earnings increase by $18 for each hour worked.
questions.correctAnswer: The earnings increase by $18 for each hour worked.
questions.explanation: Slope is change in earnings divided by change in hours, so the unit rate is dollars per hour.

questions.questionText: Triangle A has angles 43 degrees and 72 degrees. Triangle B has angles 65 degrees and 43 degrees. What connects this to side ratios?
options: AA proves the triangles are congruent, so all side lengths are equal.
AA proves the triangles are similar, so corresponding side lengths are proportional.
The triangles are unrelated because no side lengths are shown.
Only the longest sides are proportional.
questions.correctAnswer: AA proves the triangles are similar, so corresponding side lengths are proportional.
questions.explanation: Triangle A's third angle is 65 degrees. Two angle pairs match, so similarity follows and corresponding sides are proportional.

questions.questionText: A student uses points (2, 5) and (8, 17) and says the slope is 6/12. What correction is needed?
options: The student switched run and rise; the slope is 12/6 = 2.
The student should add the coordinates instead.
The slope is correct because 6/12 simplifies to 1/2.
The line has no slope because neither point is the origin.
questions.correctAnswer: The student switched run and rise; the slope is 12/6 = 2.
questions.explanation: Rise is 17 - 5 = 12 and run is 8 - 2 = 6. Slope is rise/run.

questions.questionText: Two figures have matching angles, and one side pair has scale factor 4. What must be checked before using that scale factor on every side?
options: The figures must be congruent.
The scale factor must be added to every side.
The figures must be known to be similar with correct corresponding sides.
Only the largest side pair matters.
questions.correctAnswer: The figures must be known to be similar with correct corresponding sides.
questions.explanation: A scale factor applies to all corresponding side lengths only after the similarity and side correspondence are clear.

questions.questionText: A bike moves from 4 miles to 19 miles during a 1.5 hour interval. What is the rate of change?
options: 15 miles per hour
12.7 miles per hour
23 miles per hour
10 miles per hour
questions.correctAnswer: 10 miles per hour
questions.explanation: The distance change is 15 miles. Divide by 1.5 hours to get 10 miles per hour.

questions.questionText: A dilation has scale factor 2.5. Which statement must be true about a figure and its image?
options: Corresponding angles are multiplied by 2.5.
Corresponding side lengths are multiplied by 2.5, and corresponding angles stay equal.
Only horizontal lengths are multiplied by 2.5.
The image is congruent to the original.
questions.correctAnswer: Corresponding side lengths are multiplied by 2.5, and corresponding angles stay equal.
questions.explanation: Dilations preserve angle measures and multiply all lengths by the scale factor.

questions.questionText: A line goes through (-2, 7) and (4, -5). Which slope triangle correctly represents the line from left to right?
options: rise -12 and run 6
rise 12 and run 6
rise 6 and run -12
rise -5 and run 7
questions.correctAnswer: rise -12 and run 6
questions.explanation: From x = -2 to x = 4, run is 6. y changes from 7 to -5, so rise is -12.

questions.questionText: A triangle pair has angles 30, 60, 90 and 45, 45, 90. Why is one matching right angle not enough?
options: Right triangles can never be similar.
One matching angle proves congruence instead.
The triangles are similar because all right triangles are similar.
Many non-similar right triangles share a 90 degree angle; AA needs a second matching angle pair.
questions.correctAnswer: Many non-similar right triangles share a 90 degree angle; AA needs a second matching angle pair.
questions.explanation: One angle pair is not enough. These triangles have different acute angles, so AA similarity is not proven.

questions.questionText: A graph's slope is -3/4. Which movement matches that slope?
options: up 3 and right 4
down 4 and right 3
down 3 and right 4
right 3 and down 4
questions.correctAnswer: down 3 and right 4
questions.explanation: A negative slope means the line falls from left to right. Rise/run = -3/4 means down 3, right 4.
